title: Model Painter - Fully-Vibed Mesh Texture Painting Engine for Roblox
author: Sch4k4l
selftext:
!!! First post, but I'm not a bot or an agent ;) !!!



Hey guys,



Since I don’t like the rudimentary technology of existing Roblox painting games, I decided to vibe a painting engine.

I wanted a true mesh texture painting experience with the basic tools found in painting apps.

In the public area, all 3D models can be painted and given material effects like glow, metallic, or matte/shimmer.

Players can collaborate on a painting canvas, each with their own undo and redo history.

In your own workplace, you can select models from a curated collection and save them after painting across sessions.

For your own models, there are snapshots to load previous versions, as well as a layer system typical of painting apps for multiple texture layers and combinations.

I tried out 3 GUI approaches: a desktop one-panel view and 2 mobile modes.

On phones it’s easy to paint by accident while walking/looking around. That’s why a “Walk/Paint” button at the bottom switches between moving and painting.  




[https://www.roblox.com/games/130714329911277/Model-Painter](https://www.roblox.com/games/130714329911277/Model-Painter)

I would appreciate any questions, feedback, or criticism of any kind.



Repo Overview:

* Claude Code (Anthropic, CLI; Claude Opus 4.8 to 5.5): The agent plans, implements, tests, and commits independently. To do this, it has access to files, the shell, and the MCP server.
* Markdown documentation in the repo: architecture, decisions (ADRs), plans, and instructions. This  way, the agent looks things up instead of guessing.
* In addition, there is a knowledge repository containing rules and experiences that multiple projects can read from and write to collaboratively.
* Hooks, e.g., for a memory backup or for automatic warnings when the session context is full
* Custom slash commands for recurring tasks, e.g., session handover, sending lessons to the knowledge repository, and documentation and memory optimizations



Tools used:

* Roblox Studio with MCP Server: The agent runs Luau directly in the edit, server, or client context. It starts and stops playtests, reads the console, takes screenshots, and simulates mouse and keyboard input.
* Rojo: Synchronizes scripts live from the hard drive to Studio; the map remains in Studio. Custom Studio plugins are also built using Rojo.
* Luau with --!strict
* meshy.ai and Blender: meshy.ai provides AI-generated 3D models and textures. Before uploading, a script checks the UV maps, and a Blender add-on (Python, headless) fixes them.
* Rokit specifies the versions of all tools per project. luau-lsp (type checking), selene (lint), and StyLua (formatting) run over the entire code before every commit.
* Lune: a Luau runtime outside of Roblox. This allows the core logic to be tested quickly and without Studio:
* Golden tests: the output is compared to predefined reference values
* Mutation tests: intentionally introduced errors must be detected
